### Childhood, youth and education

*See also:* [*Einstein family*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einstein_family)

⟦picture 1⟧

Einstein in 1882, age 3

Einstein was born in [Ulm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulm) as a subject to the [Kingdom of Württemberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_W%C3%BCrttemberg) in the [German Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire) on 14 March 1879. His parents, secular [Ashkenazi Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews), were [Hermann Einstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Einstein), a salesman and engineer, and [Pauline Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Koch). In 1880, the family moved to [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich)'s borough of [Ludwigsvorstadt-Isarvorstadt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwigsvorstadt-Isarvorstadt), where Einstein's father and his uncle Jakob founded Elektrotechnische Fabrik J. Einstein & Cie, a company that manufactured electrical equipment based on [direct current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_current).

When he was very young, his parents worried that he had a learning disability because he was very slow to learn to talk. When he was five and sick in bed, his father brought him a compass. This sparked his lifelong fascination with [electromagnetism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetism). He realized that "Something deeply hidden had to be behind things."

Einstein attended St. Peter's [Catholic elementary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school) in Munich from the age of five. When he was eight, he was transferred to the [Luitpold Gymnasium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luitpold_Gymnasium), where he received advanced primary and then secondary school education.

⟦picture 2⟧

⟦picture 3⟧

Einstein's parents, [Hermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Einstein) and [Pauline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Einstein)

In 1894, Hermann and Jakob's company tendered for a contract to install electric lighting in Munich, but without success—they lacked the capital that would have been required to update their technology from direct current to the more efficient, [alternating current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternating_current) alternative. The failure of their bid forced them to sell their Munich factory and search for new opportunities elsewhere. The Einstein family moved to [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy), first to [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan) and a few months later to [Pavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavia), where his father Hermann and his uncle [Jakob Einstein](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_Einstein) ran "Einstein-Garrone National Electrotechnical Workshop" ([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language): *Officine Elettrotecniche Nazionali Einstein-Garrone*) . Einstein, then fifteen, stayed behind in Munich in order to finish his schooling. His father wanted him to study [electrical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_engineering), but he was a fractious pupil who found the Gymnasium's regimen and teaching methods far from congenial. He later wrote that the school's policy of strict [rote learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rote_learning) was harmful to creativity. At the end of December 1894, a letter from a doctor persuaded the Luitpold's authorities to release him from its care, and he joined his family in Pavia. While in Italy as a teenager, he wrote an essay titled "On the Investigation of the State of the [Ether](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aether_(classical_element)>) in a Magnetic Field".

⟦picture 4⟧

Einstein family's residence from 1894-96, [Palazzo Cornazzani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palazzo_Cornazzani), Pavia.

Einstein excelled at physics and mathematics from an early age, and soon acquired the mathematical expertise normally only found in a child several years his senior. He began teaching himself [algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebra), [calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calculus) and [Euclidean geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_geometry) when he was twelve; he made such rapid progress that he discovered an original proof of the [Pythagorean theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythagorean_theorem) before his thirteenth birthday. A family tutor, [Max Talmud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Talmud), said that only a short time after he had given the twelve-year-old Einstein a geometry textbook, the boy "had worked through the whole book. He thereupon devoted himself to higher mathematics ... Soon the flight of his mathematical genius was so high I could not follow." Einstein recorded that he had "mastered [integral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral) and [differential calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_calculus)" while still just fourteen. His love of algebra and geometry was so great that at twelve, he was already confident that nature could be understood as a "mathematical structure".

⟦picture 5⟧

Einstein in 1893, age 14

At thirteen, when his range of enthusiasms had broadened to include music and philosophy, Talmud introduced Einstein to [Kant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kant)'s [*Critique of Pure Reason*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critique_of_Pure_Reason). Kant became his favorite philosopher; according to Talmud, "At the time he was still a child, only thirteen years old, yet Kant's works, incomprehensible to ordinary mortals, seemed to be clear to him."
